concepts.name: Article 14: Equality Before Law vs Equal Protection of Laws
key_dimensions: Distinction between British concept (equality before law - negative) and American concept (equal protection - positive)
Reasonable classification doctrine: intelligible differentia and rational nexus test
Landmark cases: E.P. Royappa vs State of Tamil Nadu (arbitrariness test), Maneka Gandhi case
Exception: Article 31C and its relationship with Article 14 post-Kesavananda Bharati

concepts.name: Article 14: Doctrine of Reasonable Classification
key_dimensions: Twin tests: founded on intelligible differentia and rational relation to object sought
Permissible vs impermissible classification (geographical, based on object, class legislation vs class for legislation)
UPSC trap: Classification cannot be arbitrary - Budhan Choudhry case
Application in reservation policies and special provisions for women, children, backward classes

concepts.name: Article 14: Rule of Law and Arbitrariness
key_dimensions: Dicey's three pillars of Rule of Law and Indian adoption
Arbitrariness violates Article 14 - E.P. Royappa judgment evolution
Exceptions to equality: President/Governor immunity (Article 361), foreign sovereigns
Relationship with Article 13 - laws inconsistent with fundamental rights void

concepts.name: Article 15(1) and 15(2): Prohibition of Discrimination
key_dimensions: Five grounds: religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth (UPSC trap: language NOT included)
Distinction between 15(1) - State action and 15(2) - citizens' action in public places
Scope of 'only' in Article 15(1) - allows discrimination on other reasonable grounds
Public places definition: shops, restaurants, hotels, entertainment places, wells, tanks, roads

concepts.name: Article 15(3): Special Provisions for Women and Children
key_dimensions: Not an exception but enabling provision - State 'may' make special provisions
Distinction from protective discrimination under 15(4) - not limited to backward classes
Judicial interpretation: Yusuf Abdul Aziz case, Air India vs Nargesh Meerza case
Recent applications: maternity benefits, reservation in local bodies, gender-specific welfare schemes

concepts.name: Article 15(4): Reservation for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes
key_dimensions: Added by 1st Constitutional Amendment 1951 to overcome Champakam Dorairajan judgment
SEBC definition and identification - Mandal Commission criteria
Relationship with Article 16(4) - 15(4) for educational institutions, 16(4) for public employment
UPSC trap: 15(4) is an exception to 15(1) and 29(2), not to Article 14

concepts.name: Article 15(5): Reservation in Educational Institutions
key_dimensions: Added by 93rd Amendment 2005 - enables reservation in private unaided institutions
Scope: SC/ST/SEBC in educational institutions including private aided/unaided (except minority institutions under Article 30)
Ashoka Kumar Thakur case (2008) - upheld validity with conditions
Ceiling limit: Subject to overall 50% cap established in Indra Sawhney case

concepts.name: Article 15(6): Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections
key_dimensions: Added by 103rd Constitutional Amendment 2019 - up to 10% reservation for EWS
Applies to admission in educational institutions and appointments in public employment
UPSC trap: EWS reservation is over and above 50% ceiling, applies to forward castes
Pending constitutional validity challenges and criteria for EWS identification

concepts.name: Article 16(1) and 16(2): Equality of Opportunity in Public Employment
key_dimensions: Article 16 is specific application of Article 14 in matters of public employment
16(2) prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence (UPSC trap: residence added here)
Distinction between 16(1) general equality and 16(2) specific prohibitions
Exceptions: Domicile requirement for certain state posts, physical requirements for specific jobs

concepts.name: Article 16(3): Parliament's Power to Prescribe Residence Requirement
key_dimensions: Parliament can prescribe residence requirement for certain classes of employment under a state
UPSC trap: Only Parliament can prescribe, not State Legislature
Rarely invoked provision - limited application in border states
Balance between federal structure and equality of opportunity

concepts.name: Article 16(4): Reservation for Backward Classes in Services
key_dimensions: Enabling provision for reservation in appointments/posts for backward classes not adequately represented
Indra Sawhney case (1992): 50% ceiling, creamy layer exclusion, no reservation in promotions
Subsequent amendments: 77th (Article 16(4A)), 81st (carry forward), 82nd (consequential seniority)
UPSC trap: 16(4) is not an exception but harmonious construction with 16(1)

concepts.name: Article 16(4A) and 16(4B): Reservation in Promotions and Consequential Seniority
key_dimensions: 16(4A) added by 77th Amendment 1995 - reservation in promotion for SC/ST
16(4B) added by 81st Amendment 2000 - unfilled reserved vacancies carry forward
M. Nagaraj case (2006): Creamy layer, backwardness, inadequacy of representation tests apply
Jarnail Singh case (2018): Creamy layer concept not applicable to SC/ST in promotions

concepts.name: Article 16(5): Protection of Existing Incumbents
key_dimensions: Law requiring residence within state for appointment shall not apply to existing incumbents
Protects those already in service from retrospective application
Limited scope and rarely tested provision
Distinction from Article 16(3) which deals with future appointments

concepts.name: Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability
key_dimensions: Abolishes untouchability in any form - both State and private action prohibited
Enforceable against individuals (horizontal application) unlike other fundamental rights
Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955 (earlier Untouchability Offences Act 1955) - penal provisions
UPSC trap: Practice of untouchability is an offence punishable by law, not just unenforceable

concepts.name: Article 18(1): Abolition of Titles
key_dimensions: State cannot confer titles except military and academic distinctions
UPSC trap: Bharat Ratna, Padma awards are not titles but civilian awards (Balaji Raghavan case 1995)
Prohibition applies only to titles, not awards or honors
Citizens cannot accept titles from foreign states without President's consent

concepts.name: Article 18(2): Acceptance of Foreign Titles and Honors
key_dimensions: Citizens cannot accept titles from foreign states without President's consent
Foreigners holding office of profit cannot accept without President's consent
UPSC trap: Applies to 'titles' specifically, not all foreign honors or awards
Distinction between hereditary titles (prohibited) and awards of merit (permitted)

concepts.name: Horizontal Application vs Vertical Application of Right to Equality
key_dimensions: Vertical: State action (Articles 14, 15(1), 16) vs Horizontal: Private action (Articles 15(2), 17)
Article 15(2) and 17 bind private individuals - exceptions to general rule
State definition under Article 12 and its expansive interpretation
UPSC trap: Not all equality provisions bind private parties

concepts.name: Exceptions and Limitations to Right to Equality
key_dimensions: Article 31C protection to laws giving effect to DPSPs (limited after Minerva Mills)
Article 33: Parliament's power to modify rights for armed forces
Article 34: Martial law situations
Article 361: Presidential and Gubernatorial immunity from court proceedings

concepts.name: Landmark Judgments on Right to Equality
key_dimensions: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) - led to 1st Amendment adding Article 15(4)
Indra Sawhney (1992) - 50% ceiling, creamy layer, 9-judge bench
E.P. Royappa (1974) - arbitrariness violates Article 14
Navtej Johar (2018) - Section 377, equality and dignity of LGBTQ+ persons

concepts.name: Interplay Between Articles 14, 15, 16 and Reservation Policy
key_dimensions: Article 14 permits reasonable classification, 15(4)/16(4) are specific enabling provisions
Creamy layer principle: Indra Sawhney for OBC, Jarnail Singh clarification for SC/ST
50% ceiling rule and exceptions (Tamil Nadu 69% reservation post 76th Amendment)
UPSC trap: Reservation is not fundamental right but State's enabling power for substantive equality
